key_provisions_or_claims: Robot ethics' properties approach and modestly relational approaches presuppose human-only properties such as consciousness and intelligence.
Proposes an 'eco-relational' approach embedding relationality with animals and technology in ethical concepts from the start.
Anchors properties in contexts, bodies and actions, allowing recognition of non-human agency.
Introduces hybrid actions and co-being/co-actions, e.g. robot-assisted surgery.
Technology relationships disrupt traditional ethical concepts like autonomy, agency and responsibility.
annotation.summary_en: Philosophical article arguing robot ethics is not relational enough. Critiques the properties approach and modestly relational approaches, proposing an 'eco-relational' phenomenological approach that integrates relationships with animals and robots into concepts like autonomy, agency and responsibility, leading to hybrid actions and non-human agency.
annotation.title_clean: Not Relational Enough? Towards an Eco-Relational Approach in Robot Ethics
annotation.title_en: Not Relational Enough? Towards an Eco-Relational Approach in Robot Ethics
